data.narrative:
Core Automation is a stealth-stage AI & Software company founded by Gerald Depew and Daniel C. Rozok, currently targeting a $500M–$1B Series round at a $4–5B+ post-money valuation. The broader AI & Software sector contains 16 public and private peers, though the comparable universe narrows considerably when filtered by stage and valuation tier.

Peer-median methodology is not applicable here. While 16 same-sector peers exist in AI & Software, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier companies yielded fewer than three datapoints—below the minimum threshold for reliable triangulation. The private comp set includes high-profile frontier-tech companies such as Palantir, Waymo, Figure AI, Scale AI, and Reflection AI, alongside one public reference point (Palantir, ticker PLTR). However, the heterogeneity of these firms—spanning autonomous vehicles, foundation models, data labeling, and enterprise software—limits their direct comparability to an unnamed stealth-stage platform.

Given the absence of a sufficiently dense peer cluster at Core Automation's stage and sector positioning, traditional valuation triangulation cannot be supported by the available data. The analysis would require either stage-comparable datapoints within AI & Software or additional information regarding Core Automation's revenue, growth metrics, or product-market specifics to anchor a defensible valuation range. The stated $4–5B+ target should be stress-tested against subsequent fundraising dynamics and sector-specific multiples once the company's business model and traction become observable.
